note.explanation: Pressure tells us how much normal force acts on each unit of contact area. The same force produces more pressure on a smaller area.
examples: A sharp chopper blade cuts easily because its small contact area produces high pressure.
An elephant's broad feet spread its weight over a large area, reducing pressure on the ground.
note.checkAnswer: Pressure increases when the same force acts on a smaller area.
note.simple: Pressure is force spread over an area. A smaller area means greater pressure for the same force.
note.checkQuestion: If the same force acts on a smaller area, what happens to the pressure?
note.title: Pressure
steps: Use the force acting normally on the surface for F.
Use the contact area for A.
Calculate pressure and write the unit in pascals (Pa).
note.answer: Pressure is the force exerted normally on unit area of an object. Its formula is P = F/A.

options: P = F/A
P = A/F
P = F × A
P = F + A
mcqs.stem: Which equation gives pressure when a force acts normally on a surface?
rationales: Correct: pressure is the normal force divided by the area.
Incorrect: this reverses the force and area in the pressure formula.
Incorrect: multiplying force by area does not give pressure.
Incorrect: force and area are divided, not added, to find pressure.

options: N m⁻²
N m
kg m⁻³
m² N⁻¹
mcqs.stem: What is the SI unit of pressure?
rationales: Correct: the SI unit is N m⁻², called the pascal (Pa).
Incorrect: N m is a unit of work or energy, not pressure.
Incorrect: kg m⁻³ is a unit of density.
Incorrect: m² N⁻¹ is the reciprocal of the pressure unit.

options: Pressure becomes four times as large.
Pressure becomes half as large.
Pressure stays the same.
Pressure becomes one fourth as large.
mcqs.stem: A force stays the same while its contact area is reduced to one fourth. What happens to the pressure?
rationales: Correct: since P = F/A, reducing the area to one fourth makes the pressure four times as large.
Incorrect: a smaller area increases pressure rather than reducing it.
Incorrect: pressure changes when the area changes while force stays fixed.
Incorrect: reducing area to one fourth makes pressure larger, not smaller.

options: The sharp edge has a smaller contact area, so it produces greater pressure.
The sharp edge has a larger contact area, so it produces greater pressure.
The sharp edge reduces the applied force to zero.
The sharp edge changes pressure into weight.
mcqs.stem: Why is a chopper blade made sharp?
rationales: Correct: a small contact area gives high pressure for the force applied.
Incorrect: a larger area would reduce pressure for the same force.
Incorrect: sharpening the blade does not make the applied force zero.
Incorrect: sharpening does not change pressure into weight.

options: A broad foot spreads the force over a larger area and lowers pressure.
A broad foot concentrates the force on a smaller area and raises pressure.
A broad foot removes the animal's weight.
A broad foot changes the SI unit of pressure.
mcqs.stem: Why do heavy animals such as elephants have large, flat feet?
rationales: Correct: a larger contact area reduces the pressure caused by the animal's weight.
Incorrect: a broad foot increases the contact area instead of concentrating force on a smaller one.
Incorrect: foot size does not remove an animal's weight.
Incorrect: an animal's foot size does not change pressure units.

options: The pressure is greater on the smaller contact area.
The pressure is greater on the larger contact area.
Both pressures must be zero.
Pressure does not depend on contact area.
mcqs.stem: The same normal force acts on two surfaces, but one contact area is smaller. Where is the pressure greater?
rationales: Correct: the same force divided by a smaller area gives greater pressure.
Incorrect: a larger area gives less pressure for the same force.
Incorrect: a non-zero force acting on an area produces pressure.
Incorrect: pressure depends on area according to P = F/A.

written.text: A brick measures 5 cm × 10 cm × 20 cm. If its mass is 5 kg, calculate the maximum and minimum pressure which the brick can exert on a horizontal surface.

rubric.why: Correct SI dimensions are needed to calculate the contact areas in square metres.
rubric.description: Convert the brick dimensions from centimetres to metres.

rubric.why: Pressure requires the force, which here is the brick's weight.
The two possible contact areas determine which pressure is maximum and which is minimum.
rubric.description: Find the smallest and largest face areas.
rubric.how: Use the face areas 0.005 m² and 0.02 m².

rubric.why: Both pressures and their maximum/minimum order must be correct.
rubric.description: Give the maximum and minimum pressures in the book's order.
rubric.how: Use P = F/A: the smaller area gives the maximum pressure and the larger area gives the minimum pressure.

modelAnswer: Weight of brick, F = mg = 5 × 10 = 50 N.
Possible areas = (5 × 10) cm² = 0.005 m² and (10 × 20) cm² = 0.02 m².
Maximum and minimum pressures are 1 × 10⁴ Pa and 25 × 10² Pa.

explain.title: Meaning of pressure
explain.body: Pressure is defined as the force exerted normally on unit area of an object.

explain.title: Formula and unit
explain.body: If F is the force acting normally on a surface of area A, then pressure P on the surface is given by P = F/A. The SI unit is N m⁻² and is called pascal (Pa).

explain.title: Contact area changes pressure
explain.body: The area A on which the force acts is usually referred as contact area. For a certain force, the pressure can be very large if the contact area A is small.

explain.title: Everyday examples
explain.body: A sharp chopper edge and the sharp end of a thumb pin have small contact areas, so they produce high pressure. Pebbles also reduce the foot's contact area and make walking painful. Broad, flat elephant feet increase contact area and reduce pressure.

mistakes: Writing P = A/F instead of P = F/A.
Using the wrong face area when finding maximum or minimum pressure: the smallest area gives maximum pressure.
Forgetting to convert centimetres to metres before calculating area in m².
Giving the unit as N or m² instead of Pa or N m⁻².
Saying that a larger contact area increases pressure when the force is unchanged.
